answers.question: Q14. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit, so nothing ends a read that keeps getting no answer: the customer asks to cancel HG-10482, and the order list call times out again and again while the customer waits. What ends it?
answers.recommended: The agent retries a read that gets no answer at most twice more. After the third no answer, the read counts as failed: at the start of the conversation the agent tells the customer it cannot see their orders right now and changes nothing; on the read after a cancel or refund timeout it handles it as a failed re-read.
answers.reply: > Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Q15. The cancel call can answer OrderNotFound, though the agent cancels only an order in the customer's order list. What does the agent do then?
answers.recommended: It sends no refund call, tells the customer the order could not be cancelled and that nothing was changed, and asks staff to follow up with the reason cancellation unknown.

answers.question: Q16. The refund call can answer OrderNotCancelled. What does the agent do then?
answers.recommended: It sends no second refund call, tells the customer the refund was not issued, and asks staff to follow up with the reason refund not issued.

answers.question: Q17. After a cancel timeout and a re-read that shows the order still placed or processing, the agent sends the cancel once more. What does it do if that second cancel call also gets no answer?
answers.recommended: It sends no further cancel call and no refund call, tells the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled and that no refund was made, and asks staff to follow up with the reason cancellation unknown.
